title: The Bladder That Couldn’t Hold — Parke-Davis CI-581 Patent & Domino Dissociative Anesthesia, GluN1–GluN2A/B Pore Trapping (PDB 7SAC & 7EU8), Rapid Antidepressant Trials vs. Sterile Pyuria, Contracted Bladder Compliance & Ketamine Uropathy

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Ketamine traps open NMDA channels inside brain synapses (PDB 7SAC/7EU8) to relieve anesthesia pain and severe depression, while heavy chronic urinary excretion of ketamine and norketamine strips bladder urothelium—causing sterile pyuria that mimics UTIs while scarring the bladder.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Repeatedly prescribing antibiotics for culture-negative 'UTIs' while missing high-dose ketamine exposure lets reversible bladder inflammation progress into irreversible fibrotic bladder shrinkage and kidney backup.
keyTakeaways: Synthesized as Parke-Davis CI-581 to tame phencyclidine delirium, ketamine sits inside the transmembrane pore vestibule of open GluN1–GluN2A/B NMDA receptors (PDB 7SAC, 7EU8) as a trapping channel blocker.
Controlled low-dose racemic ketamine and intranasal esketamine show rapid antidepressant efficacy under monitored protocols.
High-frequency or illicit exposure concentrates ketamine and norketamine in urine, driving ulcerative cystitis with sterile pyuria, denuded urothelium, and severely reduced bladder compliance.

vocab.meaning: When a pore blocker enters an ion channel only after agonists open the gate, then becomes trapped inside as the gate closes.
Elevated white blood cells in urine despite negative bacterial cultures—a classic clue to non-infectious inflammation like ketamine uropathy.
Change in bladder volume divided by change in detrusor pressure (dV/dP), which plummets as chronic cystitis stiffens the bladder wall.

quiz.question: Which urinary finding in a young patient with severe frequency and pelvic pain should prompt targeted LC–MS/MS or history screening for ketamine cystitis when routine bacterial cultures stay negative?
options: Persistent sterile pyuria with hematuria and contracted bladder capacity
quiz.explanation: Direct urothelial toxicity from urinary ketamine/norketamine causes intense sterile inflammation (white and red cells with negative bacterial cultures) and progressive loss of bladder capacity.
